+When [sandboxing](/docs/features/ci-features/sandboxing) is enabled, Nx tracks the files each task reads and writes. The `sandbox` property adjusts that tracking for a single target.
+Set `"enabled": false` to stop tracking a target's tasks:
+Use `ignoredReads` and `ignoredWrites` to keep tracking the target while excluding paths from its report. The patterns are globs relative to the workspace root.
+{% aside type="caution" title="Not every glob is supported" %}

+The first path segment cannot contain `*`, so `**/generated/**` is not supported. `?`, `!`, `[`, `]` and extglobs are not supported either. Nothing reports these at authoring time, so the pattern has no effect. Anchor it to a directory instead, such as `libs/*/generated/**`.

+Set `"backfill": false` to keep tracking the target but hash it from its declared inputs and outputs. By default, a recorded snapshot backfills both: the reads it observed replace the target's declared filesets, and the writes it observed extend its outputs. A target whose inputs depend on dynamic behavior or external state can't be described that way, so it should opt out.
+Reads and writes are one switch. A task hashed from its recorded reads but cached from its declared outputs would describe a run that never happened.
+`backfill` only applies where a recorded snapshot is available to read. A task hashes from its declared inputs and caches its declared outputs wherever one is not.

+A target that defines `sandbox` replaces the inherited configuration rather than adding to it. Use the [spread token](#spread-token) to merge instead, either at the object level to keep inherited keys, or inside `ignoredReads` and `ignoredWrites` to keep inherited patterns.
+{% aside type="note" title="Workspace-wide exclusions live elsewhere" %}

+`sandbox` applies to one target. To exclude paths across every task in the workspace, use `.nx/workflows/sandboxing-config.yaml`. See [Excluding paths](/docs/features/ci-features/sandboxing#excluding-paths). The two combine: a task is checked against its own `sandbox` patterns and the workspace-wide ones together, so neither overrides the other.

In the same way that `dependsOn` tells Nx to run another task before running this task, the `syncGenerator` property tells Nx to run a generator to ensure that your files are in the correct state before this task is run. [Sync generators](/docs/concepts/sync-generators) are especially useful for keeping configuration files up to date with the project graph.

Because `options[x]` and `configurations[x][y]` are the innermost levels Nx inspects, a spread token nested any deeper has no effect. For example, `options.webpack = { "...": true }` works (the spread is at `options[x]`), but `options.webpack.plugins = { "...": true }` is ignored because the spread sits inside the opaque value Nx assigns to `options.webpack`.
